name: Fiji
summary: Fiji has no fixed share for children, but the Inheritance (Family Provision) Act lets a court order provision for family left too little. Trusts exist under the Trustee Act. No private foundation law was found and the Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
family_claims: Inheritance (Family Provision) Act (Cap. 61 in the revised edition, as cited in case law): court may order provision for dependants and family. Estates are administered under the Succession, Probate and Administration Act 1970 (Cap. 60).
foreign_law_note: No choice-of-law statute was sourced. Fiji follows English common-law conflict rules (land by location, movables by domicile); not verified from a source here.
trust_note: Trustee Act (cited as Cap. 65 / Trustee Act 1966) and Public Trustee Act. Foreign trusts are recognised under common law; no trust tax regime was sourced. No private foundation law was found.
open_questions: Current title and section numbers of the family-provision statute after the 2016 revised edition.
Whether Fiji has any foundation law.
